character_sheet: A long-necked sauropod pet: four body blocks, a three-piece neck rising to a two-piece head, a four-segment tail and four two-part legs (ModelCamarasaurus.java:48-68; 21 parts on a 256x256 sheet). It is passive and tameable with an apple - one chance in two (Camarasaurus.java:201-224) - then follows its owner (:69), sits and stands on a click (:238-243), takes a name tag (:226-234) and breeds on apples (:68, :276-278); 20 HP, speed 0.2, an unused 1-damage attribute (:83-88) and no target goals at all (:76-79). It floats (:67), flees monsters (:70), panics when hurt (:72), wanders (:74) and heads indoors (:80); when hurt or now and then it browses - it walks to the nearest leaves, vine, grass, fern, cactus or tall flower within 10 blocks and, within 3.5 blocks, eats the block (mobGriefing), heals 1 and burps (:161-194), never while sitting. It spawns above y 50 by day (:295-301); a baby is drawn at half size (CamarasaurusRenderer.java:30-31). Read it as a gentle giant on a tiny hitbox: a slow four-legged stride, the neck curling to follow you, the tail swinging wide when healthy and barely when hurt.
size_notes: Drawn at x0.65 of the rig, x0.325 as a baby (CamarasaurusRenderer.java:20, 30-31) on a 256x256 sheet (ModelCamarasaurus.java:180); the hitbox is a tiny 0.5 x 1.2 under a huge model (ModEntities.java:481-484: the original's quirk, kept); shadow 0.65 x 0.65 (CamarasaurusRenderer.java:23).

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: rests 0 (front legs, back lowers) and -0.15 rad (back uppers), then pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) x the walking speed at 1.3 x 0.65 - still (rests only) below the 0.1 threshold
groups.plain: the four legs stride, upper and lower parts of a leg together: front left with back right, front right with back left
groups.math: a = limbSwingAmount > 0.1 ? cos(ageInTicks * 1.3 * 0.65) * pi * 0.25 * limbSwingAmount : 0; FLegupleft/FLegdownleft.xRot = a; FLegupright/FLegdownright.xRot = -a; BLegupleft.xRot = -0.15 - a; BLegdownleft.xRot = -a; BLegupright.xRot = -0.15 + a; BLegdownright.xRot = a
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.3 x 0.65 (wingspeed, ModelCamarasaurus.java:24): the natural period is 2 pi / 0.845 = 7.4 ticks

groups.name: tail
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad at full health, taken x 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1.0 along the chain (11 / 22 / 34 / 45 deg); BOTH the rate and the amplitude are multiplied by the health fraction (half health: 0.49 rad/tick, 22 deg at the tip)
groups.plain: the tail sweeps side to side, each segment wider than the one before - wide and quick when healthy, slow and small when hurt
groups.math: hf = health / maxHealth; n = cos(ageInTicks * 1.5 * 0.65 * hf) * pi * 0.25 * hf; Tail0.yRot = n * 0.25; Tail1.yRot = n * 0.5; Tail2.yRot = n * 0.75; Tail3.yRot = n; each segment's x/z placed along the previous segment's yaw (5, 8, 7 units)
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.5 x 0.65 x hf: the natural period at full health is 2 pi / 0.975 = 6.4 ticks

behaviour: One gait rhythm on the legs (ModelCamarasaurus.java:188-196): above a walking speed of 0.1 the cosine of the age x 1.3 x 0.65 (wingspeed, :24), x pi x 0.25, x the walking speed swings the front left and back right legs one way and the other two the opposite way - 45 degrees at full stride every 7.4 ticks, the upper and lower parts of each leg as one rigid unit (the back uppers around a -0.15 rad rest). Below the threshold the legs snap to their rests.

The tail reads the pet's health (:198-212): the health fraction multiplies both the rate (1.5 x 0.65 x hf) and the amplitude (pi x 0.25 x hf) of a sweep taken at a quarter, a half, three quarters and the whole along the four segments, each next segment's position re-derived 5, 8 and 7 units along the previous segment's yaw - an FK chain written by hand on flat bones (when this rig lands a keyframed sweep must key positions too, or the tail must be parented). At full health a 45-degree tip sweep every 6.4 ticks; near death almost still. The `if (false)` at :200-202 is dead code.

The neck and head follow the look yaw in a curl with no pitch (:214-226): the base piece takes an eighth, the middle a quarter (at the base's position), the top 0.38 (placed 6 units along the middle piece's yaw), and both head pieces the full yaw (placed 7 and 5 units along the previous piece) - so the LookAtPlayerGoal (Camarasaurus.java:73) bends the whole neck toward you. Positions again re-derived by the code.
The four body blocks never move; there is no sitting branch in the model (the synched sitting flag, toggled at Camarasaurus.java:238-243, changes nothing visible) and no attacking flag or strike.
The renderer draws it at 0.65 and a baby at half that (CamarasaurusRenderer.java:30-31) over a 0.5 x 1.2 hitbox (ModEntities.java:481-484).

formulas: `ModelCamarasaurus.poseFrom` (ModelCamarasaurus.java:192-235; orig ModelCamarasaurus.java:175-211 in `render` (func_78088_a, :169-233; func_78087_a at :241-243 is a bare super call), wingspeed 0.65 from `new ModelCamarasaurus(0.65f)` in orig ClientProxyOreSpawn.java:421): while the walking speed is above a tenth the leg swing is the cosine of the age in ticks times 1.3 times 0.65, times pi, times 0.25, times the walking speed, else 0; the front left upper and lower legs pitch by it, the front right pair by its negative, the back left upper by -0.15 minus it and its lower by minus it, the back right upper by -0.15 plus it and its lower by it. The tail sweep is the cosine of the age times 1.5 times 0.65 times the health fraction (the health over the maximum health), times pi, times 0.25, times the health fraction (the port keeps 1.7.10's sitting check as `if (false)`): the four tail segments yaw by a quarter, a half, three quarters and the whole of it, each next segment's x and z placed 5, 8 and 7 units along the previous segment's yaw (sine and cosine) from the first segment's bind pivot. The three neck pieces yaw by an eighth, a quarter and 0.38 of the look yaw in radians and the two head pieces by the whole of it; the second neck piece sits at the first's bind pivot, the third 6 units back along the second's yaw, the first head piece 7 units along the third's and the second head piece 5 units along the first head's (sine and cosine again); there is no pitch. The walk position plays no part. The GeckoLib hook is the same (CamarasaurusGeoReplacement.applyCustomAnimations).
